_what_this_is: Mechanical inventory of the corpus as it sits on disk. Facts and counts only, no interpretation. NOT the output of the Profiler agent — the .raw suffix marks this as human-reviewable source material that a person counted. Interpretation and open questions live in docs/notes/corpus-observations.md.
counting_method: every number below was measured from the extracted files; where the corpus documentation also states a number, both are recorded and compared

encoding.conclusion: UTF-8, LF only, but 32 of 1000 brat .txt files carry a UTF-8 BOM

bom_offset_interaction.finding: in the 32 BOM files the gold offsets COUNT the BOM as one character
bom_offset_interaction.implication: reading with encoding='utf-8-sig' shifts every span in those files by 1 and silently breaks 761 gold spans; read as plain 'utf-8'

pairing.brat: separate files: {docid}.txt (raw text) + {docid}.ann (standoff annotations), same basename
pairing.xml: single file per document: {docid}.xml holds TEXT in CDATA plus <TAGS> in the same file
pairing.note: both encodings of the SAME annotations are shipped; brat and xml are redundant

annotation_format.xml: i2b2-style; <MEDDOCAN><TEXT><![CDATA[...]]></TEXT><TAGS><{CATEGORY} id start end text TYPE/></TAGS></MEDDOCAN>
annotation_format.type_system_depth: brat is FLAT (one label); xml is TWO-LEVEL (coarse element name + fine TYPE attribute)

samples_verbatim._note: three raw annotation lines quoted exactly as they appear on disk, from train/brat/S0004-06142005000500011-1.ann and its .xml counterpart

samples_verbatim.surfaces_are_synthetic: MEDDOCAN patient and clinician names are synthetic replacements, not real identifiers; the corpus is CC-BY and openly published

offsets.end: exclusive — text[start:end] reproduces the annotated surface exactly
offsets.method: every gold span in train+dev+test sliced out of its .txt and compared to the surface string in the .ann
offsets.caveat: offsets index the brat .txt; the xml CDATA text is byte-identical for the documents checked
offsets.verified_spans_note: all 22795 verified while reading files as plain utf-8 (BOM retained as U+FEFF)

identifiers.document_id_format: {journal-article-id}-{n}, e.g. S0004-06142005000500011-1 — SciELO article identifier plus a per-article case number
identifiers.stem_parse_rule: stem = everything before the FINAL hyphen; case number = the trailing digits. Regex ^(?P<stem>.+)-(?P<case>\d+)$. The article part is treated as an opaque string because SciELO ids are not all-digits.

_corrected_2026_08_05.cause: The first pass parsed stems with ^(S\d{4}-\d+)-\d+$, which assumes the article part is all digits after the leading S####. 31 of 1,000 SciELO ids contain a letter — the S0465-546X, S1138-123X, S1579-699X, S1699-695X and S1889-836X journal prefixes — so those ids were dropped from the grouping entirely rather than being counted as stems.
_corrected_2026_08_05.effect: Only one of the 31 dropped ids belonged to a multi-document stem (S1889-836X2015000200005, 2 documents), which is why the stem count moved by 30 but the multi-document count moved by only 1.

identifiers.patient_id_evidence: No patient ID field exists in the annotations. Documents are published clinical case reports; each is a separate case. Patient names are annotated as NOMBRE_SUJETO_ASISTENCIA but are synthetic replacements, so they do not link documents. The article stem groups cases from the SAME journal article, which is the only observable grouping above the document.

length_distribution.tokenizer_note: whitespace split — a mechanical count, not a linguistic tokenizer
